messages:
customer-jane: hey team — since yesterday our private inference cluster in us-west-2 is timing out on streaming responses. Redwood SDK shows grpc DEADLINE_EXCEEDED after ~12s. No errors in app logs, requests reach the gateway. Can you help?

support-bot: thanks — routing to infra. @emma tagging you for visibility :mag: please advise repro steps we should ask for.

emma: on it. @customer-jane can you run from a host inside the VPC: 1) curl -v https://control.redwood.example/health 2) sudo tcpdump -i any host 10.0.5.22 and port 443 -w /tmp/rdw.pcap 3) sudo conntrack -L | grep <control-ip> and paste SG/NACL rules. short snippets are fine.

raj: quick heads-up — NACLs are stateless. A very common cause is only allowing outbound 443 but not allowing the ephemeral return-port range inbound (1024-65535). That breaks the NAT return path for long-lived streams.

customer-jane: running curl now — control health returns 200 immediately from a bastion. tcpdump shows SYN -> SYN/ACK -> then RST after ~11s when the stream should continue. attaching short pcap excerpt:
```
12:01:34.123456 IP 10.0.5.12.54321 > 3.120.45.6.443: Flags [S], seq 0
12:01:34.123567 IP 3.120.45.6.443 > 10.0.5.12.54321: Flags [S.], seq 0
12:01:45.123999 IP 3.120.45.6.443 > 10.0.5.12.54321: Flags [R], seq 1
```

liam: RST from server side after ~11s is classic for return-path problems or a middlebox killing idle flows. Do you have a TLS-inspecting appliance or an NGFW doing flow timeouts? Also paste the NACL/Security Group rules.

customer-jane: NACL outbound: ALLOW TCP 443 0.0.0.0/0 (priority 100) ; inbound: ALLOW TCP 443 0.0.0.0/0 (priority 100) ; then a DENY ALL catch-all. SG: inbound 443 from our control plane IPs, outbound ALL allowed. No managed TLS inspection that we know of.

emma: there it is — because NACLs are stateless you must explicitly allow the ephemeral port range on BOTH directions for return traffic. When NAT translates a source port to a high ephemeral port, the inbound packet uses that high port; if inbound ephemeral is denied, the responder's packets get dropped or reset. Suggested NACL change: add inbound ALLOW TCP 1024-65535 0.0.0.0/0 with a higher priority than the DENY ALL. Also ensure the outbound rules don't inadvertently restrict ephemeral range.

raj: validation commands:
- sudo conntrack -L | grep <control-ip>  # look for ESTABLISHED entries
- sudo ss -tnp | grep <control-ip>
- curl --http2 -v https://<model-host>/v1/stream --header 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' to reproduce the streaming handshake locally

customer-jane: I added inbound ALLOW TCP 1024-65535 to the NACL and re-ran the client. Replaying tcpdump shows no RST now. SDK stream is stable and completes successfully.

emma: awesome — great find. We'll update the Private deployment checklist to call this out (NACL stateless return ports). I'll follow up with a short KB and include the conntrack commands and a sample fix. :white_check_mark:

support-bot: Escalation closed — customer-confirmed fix. Tagging #postmortems and marking for docs update.
